web.auth.intro.body: operon runs on your own computer, right next to your code and your AI coding agents. Sign in to drive them from any browser — chat, review diffs, run terminals and manage tasks — while everything keeps executing on your machine.
web.auth.login.desc: Connect your account to reach and control the machines running operon.
web.auth.login.reviewerHint: For App Store review. Use the credentials from the review notes.
web.auth.login.title: Sign in
web.auth.noMachines: No machines yet. Open the operon app on your computer and connect it to the SaaS, then refresh.
web.auth.noMachines.otherProvider: You are signed in with {current}. Signing in with {other} creates a separate account — if you paired your machine that way, sign out and use {other} instead.
web.auth.nodeOffline.desc: Open operon on the selected machine, then refresh or choose another machine.
web.auth.nodeOffline.title: Machine offline
web.deleteAccount.failed: Couldn't delete your account. Try again.
web.deleteAccount.item.account: Your account and the sign-in identities linked to it.
web.deleteAccount.item.localData: Your projects, files and conversations live on your own machines and are not touched — operon never stored them.
web.deleteAccount.item.machines: Every paired machine, and any device registered for notifications.
web.deleteAccount.item.sessions: All active sessions. This cannot be undone.
web.deleteAccount.signedOut: Sign in to operon first, then open More → Delete account. The same option is in the mobile app.
web.deleteAccount.subtitle: Delete your account
workflow.tab.title: Workflow
workspace.new.desc: Create a new isolated workspace for your changes.
workspace.new.title: New Workspace
workspace.new.worktreeHint: Created under operon's managed worktrees folder (~/.operon/worktrees), not next to your project.
